sql:
SELECT z.LocationID, z.Zone
FROM ops.zones z
WHERE z.LocationID NOT IN (SELECT t.RatecodeID FROM lake.trips t WHERE t.PULocationID = z.LocationID)
ORDER BY z.LocationID

diagnosis.bottleneck: The optimizer chose a costly LEFT_DELIM_JOIN with a HASH_JOIN subtree that scans the 495K-row trips table and builds a hash table on RatecodeID, triggered by the NOT IN subquery with a correlated equality predicate on PULocationID; the DELIM_SCAN (node 8) indicates row-by-row subquery evaluation for each zone row.

hypotheses.claim: NOT IN over a subquery forces a null-aware anti join, which is expensive. (matched: not in (select t.ratecodeid from lake.trips t where t.pulocationid = z.locationid) order b)
The LEFT_DELIM_JOIN executes the subquery once per zones row (265 times) because the NOT IN with a correlated reference prevents decorrelation, causing repeated scans of trips.

The inner HASH_JOIN builds a hash table on RatecodeID from the full trips scan (495K rows) for each zones row, which is redundant since the join key PULocationID = LocationID could be pushed into a single semi/anti join.
The DELIM_SCAN with Estimated Cardinality 167 reflects the per-iteration overhead of the correlated subquery execution, confirming the row-by-row evaluation pattern.
